question: to the Commission Adnan Dibrani (S&D), Laura Ballarín Cereza (S&D), Andreas Schieder (S&D), Yvan Verougstraete (Renew), Erik Marquardt (Verts/ALE), Rasmus Andresen (Verts/ALE), Bruno Gonçalves (S&D), Heléne Fritzon (S&D), Johan Danielsson (S&D), Evin Incir (S&D), Sofie Eriksson (S&D), Nikola Minchev (Renew), Christel Schaldemose (S&D), Hannes Heide (S&D), René Repasi (S&D), Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Emma Rafowicz (S&D), Marc Angel (S&D), Pierfrancesco Maran (S&D), Diana Riba i Giner (Verts/ALE), Elisabeth Grossmann (S&D), Tonino Picula (S&D), Biljana Borzan (S&D), Elena Sancho Murillo (S&D), Lara Wolters (S&D), Maria Grapini (S&D), Daniel Attard (S&D), Hanna Gedin (The Left), Sakis Arnaoutoglou (S&D), Katarina Barley (S&D), Sérgio Gonçalves (S&D), Anna Cavazzini (Verts/ALE), Gordan Bosanac (Verts/ALE), Niels Fuglsang (S&D), Carolina Morace (The Left), Lídia Pereira (PPE) Subject:

Ticket sales for the 2026 FIFA World Cup have renewed concerns about dynamic pricing, with some tickets reaching prices of USD 30 000. Media sources have described it as the most expensive World Cup in football history. Dynamic pricing relies on algorithms that adjust prices in real time based on demand. Such practices risk undermining transparency, consumer trust and fair access to major sporting and cultural events. When prices are changed continuously by algorithms that consumers cannot scrutinise, markets risk becoming opaque and unfair. In the light of the upcoming 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain, Portugal and Morocco and the growing use of dynamic pricing across the live events sector: 1.

Does the Commission consider the current EU framework to be sufficient to protect consumers from excessive and unpredictable price increases caused by dynamic pricing, or will it propose additional transparency requirements and consumer safeguards?

Will the Commission investigate whether the use of dynamic pricing by dominant ticketing platforms could distort competition or constitute an abuse of a dominant position under Article 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union?

Ahead of the 2030 World Cup, will the Commission take action on dynamic pricing for major sporting and cultural events, including by considering restricting or, where necessary, prohibiting such practices?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.9.2026) EU consumer protection rules do not prevent price changes by market operators, including in the event ticketing sector and when implemented via dynamic pricing. Consumers are protected by the transparency requirements of the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive1 (UCPD) and the Consumer Rights Directive2 (CRD). Furthermore, the UCPD prohibits misleading practices. EU consumer law directives are transposed into national law. Member States’ authorities and courts are responsible for enforcement in individual cases, including as in the context of major sporting and cultural events. The Commission may propose in the upcoming Digital Fairness Act3 additional rules regarding price marketing. Dynamic pricing by dominant undertakings can fall within the scope of Article 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union if it amounts to the imposition of excessive prices. However, whether pricing is excessive depends on the relationship between a dominant undertaking’s costs and profits rather than on pricing mechanisms. The Commission has in the past investigated excessive pricing by dominant undertakings including in the pharmaceutical and energy sectors4. The Commission remains vigilant as regards possible excessive pricing abuses and stands ready to intervene in appropriate cases also in light of its priorities5. Through policies and programmes including Erasmus+, the Commission promotes a European Sport Model grounded in values such as fairness and solidarity. The upcoming Commission Communication on ‘A Strategic Vision for Sport in Europe: Reinforcing the European Sport Model’ aims to strengthen good governance principles, notably stakeholder representation including fans6.

1 Directive 2005/29/EC, http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj. 2 Directive 2011/83/EU, http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/83/oj. 3 Subject to the impact assessment, the Commission plans to propose the Digital Fairness Act in the fourth

quarter of 2026, for more information: https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-yoursay/initiatives/14622-Digital-Fairness-Act_en. 4 Case AT.40394 - Aspen; and case AT. 39816 - Upstream gas supplies in Central and Eastern Europe. In both cases, the Commission accepted commitments by the dominant undertaking that allowed bringing prices to lower, competitive levels. 5 For completeness, the Commission has received a complaint by Euroconsumers and Football Supporters Europe, which alleges that the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) abused its dominant position by imposing excessive ticket prices as well as opaque and unfair purchasing conditions on European fans ahead of the 2026 World Cup. The Commission is examining the complaint in line with the applicable rules and cannot comment on ongoing cases. 6 For more information: https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/14741-Astrategic-vision-for-sport-in-Europe-reinforcing-the-European-Sport-Model/public-consultation_en.
